symbols.name: integer to invert
symbols.meaning: The integer whose inverse modulo $M$ is sought.
symbols.quote: Here $\beta$ is the integer to be inverted, $M \ge 1$ is the modulus, and $\mu$ is the inverse: an inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.

symbols.name: modulus
symbols.meaning: A positive integer, the modulus of the congruence.
symbols.quote: Here $\beta$ is the integer to be inverted, $M \ge 1$ is the modulus, and $\mu$ is the inverse: an inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.

symbols.name: modular inverse
symbols.meaning: The integer with $\beta\mu$ congruent to $1$ modulo $M$.
symbols.quote: Here $\beta$ is the integer to be inverted, $M \ge 1$ is the modulus, and $\mu$ is the inverse: an inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.

symbols.name: multiple of the modulus
symbols.meaning: The integer with $\beta\mu - 1 = \nu M$ in a solution of the congruence.
symbols.quote: If $\beta\mu \equiv 1 \pmod M$, then $\beta\mu - 1 = \nu M$ for some integer $\nu$, so every common divisor of $\beta$ and $M$ divides $1$.

symbols.name: product of the lengths
symbols.meaning: The product $M_1 M_2 \cdots$ of all the lengths, the order of the cyclic group.
symbols.quote: Put $S = M_1 M_2 \cdots$ for their product, and $\pi_i = M_1 M_2 \cdots M_{i-1}$ for the product of the earlier lengths, with $\pi_1 = 1$.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The $i$-th of the pairwise coprime lengths, the number of entries along one cyclic axis.
symbols.quote: Here $M_i$ denotes the length of the $i$-th axis, for $i = 1, 2, \dots$, and the letter $i$ indexes them only in this paragraph.

symbols.name: prefix product
symbols.meaning: The product of the lengths before the $i$-th, so $\pi_1 = 1$.
symbols.quote: Put $S = M_1 M_2 \cdots$ for their product, and $\pi_i = M_1 M_2 \cdots M_{i-1}$ for the product of the earlier lengths, with $\pi_1 = 1$.

symbols.name: exponent of an axis
symbols.meaning: The inverse of $\pi_i$ modulo $M_i$, used as the exponent of $\xi_i$.
symbols.quote: Each $\pi_i$ is coprime to $M_i$, so the inverse $\mu_i$ of $\pi_i$ modulo $M_i$ exists.

symbols.name: cyclic generator
symbols.meaning: A generator of a cyclic group of order $S$, which the map sends to $\prod_i \xi_i^{\mu_i}$.
symbols.quote: The paper's map sends the generator $\xi$ of a cyclic group of order $S$ to $\prod_i \xi_i^{\mu_i}$, where $\xi_i$ generates a cyclic group of order $M_i$, so $\xi_i^{M_i} = 1$.

symbols.name: axis generator
symbols.meaning: A generator of the cyclic group of order $M_i$ on the $i$-th axis.
symbols.quote: The paper's map sends the generator $\xi$ of a cyclic group of order $S$ to $\prod_i \xi_i^{\mu_i}$, where $\xi_i$ generates a cyclic group of order $M_i$, so $\xi_i^{M_i} = 1$.

relations.quote: Here $\beta$ is the integer to be inverted, $M \ge 1$ is the modulus, and $\mu$ is the inverse: an inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.
An inverse of $\beta$ modulo $M$ exists exactly when $\beta$ and $M$ are [coprime](coprime.md).
